quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Clean Sweep Cleaners now offers a pick-up service for customers who are too busy to visit the shop. Customers can order through the website before 9 a.m., and their clothes are collected the same day. The clean clothes are returned within forty-eight hours. The service costs an extra three dollars per order.
quests.question: A customer who orders at 8 a.m. can have clothes collected that day.
quests.hint: Compare the order time with the deadline.
quests.explanation: Orders placed before 9 a.m. are collected the same day, and 8 a.m. is before that deadline.
quests.evidenceLine: Customers can order through the website before 9 a.m., and their clothes are collected the same day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Polar bears are excellent swimmers and can travel long distances between pieces of sea ice. Their thick layer of fat keeps them warm in freezing water. Despite their white appearance, their fur is actually transparent and their skin is black. Scientists believe that black skin helps them absorb heat from the sun.
quests.question: Polar bears have white skin that reflects sunlight.
quests.hint: Read what the passage says about the skin.
quests.explanation: The passage says the skin is black, and it is thought to absorb heat.
quests.evidenceLine: Despite their white appearance, their fur is actually transparent and their skin is black.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Dear parents, the school trip to the science museum has been moved from Tuesday to Thursday because of a bus strike. Students should still bring a packed lunch and wear comfortable shoes. The cost of the trip will not change. Please return the signed permission form by Wednesday morning.
quests.question: Families will pay the same price for the trip as before.
quests.hint: Find the sentence about money.
quests.explanation: The cost will not change, so the price stays the same.
quests.evidenceLine: The cost of the trip will not change.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Many people believe that cracking their knuckles causes arthritis. Studies that compared long-term knuckle crackers with people who never did it found no difference in arthritis rates. The popping sound comes from gas bubbles in the fluid around the joints. Doctors say the habit is usually harmless, although it can annoy other people.
quests.question: Studies found similar arthritis rates in knuckle crackers and non-crackers.
quests.hint: Look at what the studies compared.
quests.explanation: Both groups had similar arthritis rates, so no link was found.
quests.evidenceLine: Studies that compared long-term knuckle crackers with people who never did it found no difference in arthritis rates.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: For your safety, please do not use the pool if a thunderstorm is nearby. Lifeguards will blow a whistle when lightning is seen within ten kilometers, and everyone must leave the water immediately. The pool will reopen thirty minutes after the last thunder is heard. Swimmers may wait in the changing rooms.
quests.question: Swimmers must get out of the water as soon as lightning is spotted close by.
quests.hint: Focus on the whistle rule for swimmers.
quests.explanation: Lightning within ten kilometers means everyone leaves the water immediately.
quests.evidenceLine: Lifeguards will blow a whistle when lightning is seen within ten kilometers, and everyone must leave the water immediately.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Many adults think it is too late to learn a language well. However, research shows that adults often learn grammar and vocabulary faster than children. Where children usually do better is in copying the accent of native speakers. Adults, on the other hand, can use study techniques that children do not know.
quests.question: Adults usually copy a native accent better than children do.
quests.hint: Find the area where children have the advantage.
quests.explanation: Children usually do better at copying an accent, so the statement is reversed.
quests.evidenceLine: Where children usually do better is in copying the accent of native speakers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Hello Mr. Haddad, we are pleased to confirm your booking at the Lakeside Hotel for three nights, starting on June 14. Check-in is possible from 2 p.m., and breakfast is served between 7 and 10 a.m. If you arrive after 10 p.m., please tell us in advance. Free parking is available for guests.
quests.question: Breakfast at the hotel is served until noon.
quests.hint: Look for the breakfast hours.
quests.explanation: Breakfast ends at 10 a.m., not at noon.
quests.evidenceLine: Check-in is possible from 2 p.m., and breakfast is served between 7 and 10 a.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The Great Wall of China was not built all at once. Different rulers added and repaired sections over many centuries, and some parts are more than two thousand years old. Much of the wall that tourists visit today was built during the Ming dynasty, which ended in 1644. It is a series of walls rather than a single line.
quests.question: The whole Great Wall was completed under a single ruler.
quests.hint: Ask who built the wall and over how long.
quests.explanation: The wall was built in stages by different rulers over many centuries.
quests.evidenceLine: The Great Wall of China was not built all at once. Different rulers added and repaired sections over many centuries, and some parts are more than two thousand years old.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Priyanka's cousins are visiting from Canada for two weeks. Her parents have organized a trip to the mountains for the weekend, and the whole family will travel in two cars. Priyanka is excited because she has not seen her cousins for three years. She has already prepared a list of games to play in the evening.
quests.question: Priyanka last saw her cousins three years ago.
quests.hint: Look for why Priyanka is excited.
quests.explanation: She has not seen them for three years, so the last visit was three years ago.
quests.evidenceLine: Priyanka is excited because she has not seen her cousins for three years.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Orchids are among the largest families of flowering plants, with more than twenty-five thousand known species. Many grow on tree branches rather than in soil, taking water from the humid air with special roots. Because they are so delicate, orchids are often grown indoors. Growers advise keeping them away from direct midday sun.
quests.question: There are fewer than ten thousand known orchid species.
quests.hint: Check the number in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage gives more than twenty-five thousand species, far above ten thousand.
quests.evidenceLine: Orchids are among the largest families of flowering plants, with more than twenty-five thousand known species.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: When you heat a metal rod, it expands slightly because its particles move faster and take up more space. Engineers must consider this when they build bridges and railways. Small gaps are left between sections of track so that the rails do not bend on hot days. In cold weather, the metal contracts and the gaps grow wider.
quests.question: In cold weather, the gaps between track sections become narrower.
quests.hint: Think about how metal behaves in the cold.
quests.explanation: The metal contracts in the cold, so the gaps get wider rather than narrower.
quests.evidenceLine: In cold weather, the metal contracts and the gaps grow wider.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Traditional Italian tomato sauce takes only a few ingredients, but the cooking time is important. The tomatoes should simmer gently for at least forty-five minutes so that the flavor becomes rich and slightly sweet. Adding a pinch of sugar can reduce sharpness, although good tomatoes rarely need it. Fresh basil is added at the very end.
quests.question: The basil goes into the sauce last.
quests.hint: Look at when the basil is added.
quests.explanation: The final sentence says fresh basil is added at the very end.
quests.evidenceLine: Fresh basil is added at the very end.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Ants communicate mainly through chemical signals called pheromones. When an ant finds food, it leaves a scent trail on the way back to the nest. Other ants follow the trail and strengthen it with their own scent. When the food runs out, the trail disappears because no more ants refresh it.
quests.question: The scent trail fades because ants stop renewing it.
quests.hint: Find the reason the trail disappears.
quests.explanation: The trail vanishes when no more ants refresh it.
quests.evidenceLine: When the food runs out, the trail disappears because no more ants refresh it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A small furniture company in Poland has doubled its sales in two years after moving most of its business online. The owner says that customers now send photos of their rooms, and designers suggest suitable pieces. The company has hired eight more employees. It still keeps one small shop for customers who want to see the furniture in person.
quests.question: The company has kept a physical shop.
quests.hint: Read the final sentence.
quests.explanation: One small shop remains for customers who want to see the furniture in person.
quests.evidenceLine: It still keeps one small shop for customers who want to see the furniture in person.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Valentina's grandfather taught her to play chess when she was six. They played every Sunday afternoon, and he never let her win on purpose. Now Valentina is fifteen and plays in tournaments, while her grandfather prefers watching from the audience. She says his patience taught her more than any book.
quests.question: Valentina's grandfather often let her win when she was little.
quests.hint: How did the grandfather play against her?
quests.explanation: He never let her win on purpose, which is the opposite.
quests.evidenceLine: They played every Sunday afternoon, and he never let her win on purpose.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The human body contains about sixty percent water. The brain and heart are even more watery, at around seventy-three percent, while bones contain about thirty-one percent. Because water is constantly lost through breathing, sweating, and waste, people need to replace it. Thirst is one signal that the body needs more.
quests.question: Bones contain more water than the brain does.
quests.hint: Compare the percentages for bones and the brain.
quests.explanation: The brain is around seventy-three percent water and bones about thirty-one percent.
quests.evidenceLine: The brain and heart are even more watery, at around seventy-three percent, while bones contain about thirty-one percent.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sunscreen protects the skin from harmful ultraviolet rays. Experts recommend applying it about fifteen minutes before going outside and reapplying every two hours. Reapplication is even more important after swimming or heavy sweating, because water washes the protection away. Cloudy days do not remove the need, since UV rays pass through clouds.
quests.question: Sunscreen is unnecessary on cloudy days.
quests.hint: Read the last sentence about clouds.
quests.explanation: UV rays pass through clouds, so protection is still needed.
quests.evidenceLine: Cloudy days do not remove the need, since UV rays pass through clouds.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: At the start of the semester, Professor Khan asks every student to choose a topic for a long research paper. Students then meet with her once a month to discuss their progress. The final paper counts for forty percent of the course grade. The remaining sixty percent comes from two exams.
quests.question: The two exams together count for more of the grade than the paper does.
quests.hint: Compare the percentage for the paper with the rest.
quests.explanation: The paper is worth forty percent and the exams the remaining sixty.
quests.evidenceLine: The final paper counts for forty percent of the course grade. The remaining sixty percent comes from two exams.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Starting next month, the city will introduce a new bus schedule on routes 4 and 9. Buses will now run every ten minutes during rush hour instead of every twenty. During the evening, service will continue to run every twenty minutes until midnight. The changes are part of a plan to reduce traffic in the city center.
quests.question: Buses will come less often during rush hour than before.
quests.hint: Compare the old and new rush-hour intervals.
quests.explanation: Every ten minutes is more frequent than every twenty.
quests.evidenceLine: Buses will now run every ten minutes during rush hour instead of every twenty.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Elena Marek's first novel took her eight years to finish. She wrote in the evenings after work and rewrote the first chapter more than twenty times. When the book was finally published, it sold out within a week. Elena now writes full time but says she misses the calm of her old routine.
quests.question: Elena Marek finished her first novel in less than a year.
quests.hint: Look at how long the novel took.
quests.explanation: The novel took eight years, not less than one.
quests.evidenceLine: Elena Marek's first novel took her eight years to finish.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, but they support about a quarter of all marine species. Rising water temperatures cause corals to lose their color, a process called bleaching. Bleached corals are not dead, but they are weak and may die if the heat continues. Protecting reefs, therefore, means reducing the heat as well as pollution.
quests.question: Bleached corals are already dead.
quests.hint: Read what the passage says about bleached corals.
quests.explanation: They are described as weak but not dead.
quests.evidenceLine: Bleached corals are not dead, but they are weak and may die if the heat continues.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: When we arrived in Lisbon, our luggage did not arrive with us. The airline promised to deliver it to the hotel within a day, and the staff gave us a small kit with toothbrushes and T-shirts. We spent the first afternoon buying clothes. The suitcases finally appeared the next morning.
quests.question: The travelers' suitcases arrived the following morning.
quests.hint: When did the suitcases turn up?
quests.explanation: The last sentence says the suitcases appeared the next morning.
quests.evidenceLine: The suitcases finally appeared the next morning.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Nora used to check her email every few minutes while she worked. Then she read that constant interruptions make it harder to focus, so she now checks it only three times a day. She says the change was difficult at first. After two weeks, she noticed that she finished her tasks earlier.
quests.question: Nora now checks her email less often than before.
quests.hint: Compare her old and new habits.
quests.explanation: She went from every few minutes to three times a day.
quests.evidenceLine: Then she read that constant interruptions make it harder to focus, so she now checks it only three times a day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Casa Verde offers a vegetarian tasting menu with five small dishes. Each dish is prepared with vegetables from the restaurant's own garden. Meat-eating guests are often surprised by how filling the meal is. The chef changes the menu every month. Vegetarian guests can also ask for a smaller portion.
quests.question: The restaurant grows some of the vegetables it serves.
quests.hint: Where do the vegetables come from?
quests.explanation: They come from the restaurant's own garden.
quests.evidenceLine: Each dish is prepared with vegetables from the restaurant's own garden.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Before buying a used sofa, experts suggest checking the frame by lifting one corner. If the other legs stay on the floor, the frame is probably twisted. A good sofa also has firm cushions that return to their shape when pressed. Buyers should ask whether the covers can be washed.
quests.question: A sofa is in good condition if its cushions stay flat after being pressed.
quests.hint: Focus on how good cushions respond to pressure.
quests.explanation: Good cushions return to their shape, so flat cushions are a bad sign.
quests.evidenceLine: A good sofa also has firm cushions that return to their shape when pressed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Lavender grows best in dry, sunny places with poor soil. Too much water or rich soil makes the plant produce more leaves but fewer flowers. Gardeners in wet climates often plant it in raised beds with sand mixed in. The flowers attract bees and are also used for making oil.
quests.question: Rich soil can reduce the number of flowers on a lavender plant.
quests.hint: Look at what rich soil does to the plant.
quests.explanation: Rich soil produces more leaves but fewer flowers.
quests.evidenceLine: Too much water or rich soil makes the plant produce more leaves but fewer flowers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In Sweden, many workplaces have a daily coffee break called fika. It is not simply a pause for a drink but a chance for colleagues to talk and relax together. Managers often join in, and skipping it may be seen as unfriendly. Visitors to Swedish offices are usually invited to take part.
quests.question: Fika is meant to be social time as well as a coffee break.
quests.hint: Read the purpose of the break.
quests.explanation: It is a chance for colleagues to talk and relax together.
quests.evidenceLine: It is not simply a pause for a drink but a chance for colleagues to talk and relax together.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The new drama series begins with a car accident, but it is not an action show. Most of its eight episodes take place in a small kitchen, where the characters slowly reveal their secrets. Critics have praised the acting but complained that the plot moves too slowly in the middle. Viewers seem to disagree, since the series has been streamed millions of times.
quests.question: Critics found the middle of the series slow.
quests.hint: Look for the critics' complaint.
quests.explanation: They said the plot moves too slowly in the middle.
quests.evidenceLine: Critics have praised the acting but complained that the plot moves too slowly in the middle.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Dear staff, from next Monday, the office will introduce a hot-desk system. Nobody will have a fixed desk, and everyone must book a place through the company app before arriving. Personal items should be kept in the lockers provided. The system is designed to save space, because on average only sixty percent of desks were used each day.
quests.question: Every employee will keep a permanent desk under the new system.
quests.hint: Check the fate of fixed desks.
quests.explanation: Nobody will have a fixed desk, so permanent desks end.
quests.evidenceLine: Nobody will have a fixed desk, and everyone must book a place through the company app before arriving.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Cyclists in a long race often ride close together in a group called the peloton. The riders at the front work hardest because they break the wind for the others. Teams take turns at the front so that no one becomes too tired. A rider sheltered in the middle of the group uses much less energy.
quests.question: The riders at the back of the group work the hardest.
quests.hint: Which riders take the wind?
quests.explanation: The riders at the front break the wind and work hardest.
quests.evidenceLine: The riders at the front work hardest because they break the wind for the others.
